findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the sort key. With order_by='-datetime' in the audit logs endpoint, that key is a datetime, so a TypeError is raised. DateTimePaginator avoids this by converting to an epoch timestamp first.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor.value without converting it back to a datetime as DateTimePaginator does. build_queryset therefore compares a datetime field against an integer on subsequent pages.

The enable_advanced check in the audit logs endpoint accesses organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check. member is None for callers without membership, such as superusers, API keys/org auth tokens, legacy org ApiKeys and internal-integration proxy users, so an AttributeError is raised.

When enable_advanced_features is true, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes a user-supplied negative cursor.offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so a crafted cursor (e.g. 0:-10:0) raises an error that is not converted to BadPaginationError and results in a 500.

Comments and docstrings in the patch contain false or marketing-style claims. Examples are that the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing, 'sophisticated pagination patterns', and 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level'.

The change to the shared BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative next-cursor offsets to 0 with max(0, offset). Negative prev-cursor offsets still reach the queryset slice and raise errors, which contradicts the comment saying negative offsets are allowed.
BasePaginator.get_result uses start_offset = max(0, offset) for slicing but still uses the raw offset in the duplicate-trim check (len(results) == offset + limit + extra), so the two diverge.
The comments added to the Cursor class in cursors.py say negative offsets are now allowed or optimized. No code in Cursor changed, and int(offset) already accepted negative values.

OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near line-for-line copy of BasePaginator.get_result and Paginator's key/cursor methods, plus broken additions. It builds the same queryset, makes the same count call and uses the same slice, so it does not deliver the claimed performance improvement.
No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator, the optimized_pagination=true endpoint branch and its cursor handling, or the change to BasePaginator.get_result.
The patch adds trailing whitespace and extra blank lines at end of file, which fail the repo's trailing-whitespace and end-of-file-fixer pre-commit hooks.
The endpoint's if/else block repeats the same self.paginate(...) call, differing only in paginator_cls and one kwarg.
The enable_advanced_features constructor flag has a single caller that always passes True. Its name does not indicate that it enables negative-offset slicing.
The code imports OptimizedCursorPaginator, which does not exist.

The admin gate checks the raw request.user.is_superuser DB flag instead of is_active_superuser(request), which bypasses the active superuser-session check. has_global_access also defaults to True for members, so the gate does not restrict access to admins.
The new optimized_pagination query parameter is not documented in the API docs or changelog.
